name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Log every prompt change in a shared log with timestamps and exact text—no exceptions. This guarantees we can trace why a prompt performed differently, spot regressions, and reuse winning variants. The trade-off is extra upfront work, but it pays off when debugging or iterating. Without it, we risk repeating mistakes or losing context when prompts evolve.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn't the extra upfront work, but rather that logging every tweak without filtering will drown the signal in noise, making it harder to identify meaningful changes. A better alternative would be to implement a selective logging system that only records significant prompt changes, such as those that result in substantial performance improvements or declines. This argument could be settled by experimenting with both approaches and comparing the efficiency of debugging and iteration in each case.
